html:
A 1972 song by the Cameroonian saxophonist Manu Dibango that became an international hit and one of the most sampled African records.

It was first released in Cameroon as the B side of a song for the national team at the Africa Cup of Nations, which Cameroon hosted in 1972. Its mix of makossa, a dance music of the port city of Douala, with funk and jazz caught the ear of DJs in New York clubs. In 1973 it reached the American pop charts, one of the first African songs to do so, and it helped shape early disco.

Its chant, "mama-ko, mama-sa, ma-ma-ko-ssa", had a long life. Michael Jackson used it in "Wanna Be Startin' Somethin'" in 1982, and Rihanna in 2007. Dibango took legal action over the uses and settled. He kept performing until he died of COVID-19 in 2020.
sum: A 1972 song by the Cameroonian saxophonist Manu Dibango that became an international hit and one of the most sampled African records.
